articles.title: Friday blockbuster for Jio IPO: Rs 7.4 lakh crore bids, 22x subscription
articles.description: Mumbai: Jio Platforms' mega initial public offering (IPO), the largest in Indian corporate history, drew aggregate bids worth about ₹7.41 lakh crore, closing on Friday with an overall subscription of 22.19 times in public bids. The strong response, especially from institutional investors, was in sharp contrast to the weak secondary-market sentiment amid mounting concerns over elevated crude oil prices and foreign-fund selling. Investors across categories sought to buy 4.38 billion shares in public bids, against 197.5 million shares on offer, combined data from both stock exchanges showed.135160349Public bids over the past three days totalled ₹4.91 lakh crore at the higher end of the price band at ₹1,119 a share. The public issue, which had opened Wednesday, closed for subscription Friday. The stock would list on October 28. Along with the anchor book, where global and domestic bulge-bracket investors bid more than ₹2.5 lakh crore, the total bid value for the 30,213-crore IPO was ₹7.41 lakh crore. Read more: Jio IPO breaks 12 records: Rs 4.5 lakh crore bids, highest applications and moreJio had allotted shares worth ₹8,109.85 crore to anchor investors at ₹1,119 a share, with domestic mutual funds accounting for 34.34% of the anchor book allocation. Institutional investors led the demand in the IPO bidding process. The qualified institutional buyers' (QIB) portion was subscribed 70.55 times, receiving bids for 3.46 billion shares against 49 million shares reserved for the category. Domestic financial institutions, including banks and insurance companies, bid for 1.52 billion shares, while foreign institutional investors bid for 1.24 billion shares. Mutual funds bid for 357 million shares, and other investors in the QIB category bid for 336.2 million shares. Read more: Jio IPO ends with over 22X oversubscription; QIB portion booked 70 times. Check GMP, other detailsThe non-institutional investor (NII) segment was subscribed 14 times, with bids for 510 million shares against 36.4 million shares reserved for the category. Within this segment, investors bidding for more than ₹10 lakh subscribed their portion 15.89 times, while the category for bids between ₹2 lakh and ₹10 lakh was subscribed 10.21 times. Retail investors bid for 231.1 million shares against 85 million shares reserved for them, taking subscription to 2.72 times. The employee portion was subscribed 2.93 times, while the shareholder quota received bids for 169.7 million shares against 22.3 million shares on offer, translating into 7.60 times subscription. The IPO was fully subscribed within about 100 minutes of opening, led by institutional demand. The IPO was priced in the band of ₹1,065-1,119 per share. The entire IPO of Jio Platforms, the digital and telecom arm of Reliance Industries led by Mukesh Ambani, has been through a fresh share issue with no offer-for-sale component.

articles.title: Small and midcap indices post worst weekly decline in two years
articles.description: Mumbai: The current bout of sell-off in mid-cap and small-cap stocks deepened Friday, with respective indices posting their worst weekly declines in two years, as the rout threatens to unravel one of the rare pockets in Indian equities that remained relatively unscathed in the face of an attritional blue-chip retreat since late 2024. Hence, the latest weakness has stoked concerns that the protracted risk-off sentiment in blue-chips may now be spreading to the broader markets, potentially denting the confidence of retail investors whose steady contributions to mutual funds have helped undergird the theoretically riskier end of the equity spectrum amid waning overseas interest in frontliners and a sliding currency.135160209The Nifty MidCap 150 fell 2.1%, and the Small-cap 250 dropped 2.8% on Friday. The BSE Sensex fell 125.56 points, or 0.17%, to close at 73,123.83, while the NSE Nifty 50 declined 87.65 points, or 0.39%, to end at 22,600, erasing a portion of the early losses. The main indices had fallen more than 1% earlier in the day. For the week, the Nifty Midcap 150 fell 5.26%, recording the worst seven-day fall since October 2024, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 declined 7.10%, registering the worst weekly fall since February 2025. Friday's sell-off led to the market capitalisation of all BSE-listed companies falling 1.42% or ₹6.54 lakh crore to ₹453.45 lakh crore. In the last week, the market cap has fallen by 4.38% or ₹20.78 lakh crore. Read more: Jio IPO breaks 12 records: Rs 4.5 lakh crore bids, highest applications and more"Markets are driven by flows, sentiment and fundamentals, and there is high supply from FPIs as well as IPOs," said Nilesh Shah, Managing Director, Kotak Mahindra Asset Management. "Sentiment due to the current calendar year's negative returns and due to unmet expectations of tax concessions is poor."So far in 2026, the Sensex and Nifty have retreated 14.2% and 13.2%, respectively. The Mid-cap 150 has declined 7%, while the Small-cap 250 has dropped 1.8%. Before this week, both broad market indices were sitting on gains, as domestic retail investors showed faith in the smaller shares, pouring record money into these segments through equity mutual fund schemes.REASONABLE VALUATIONSThe correction is not an earnings collapse but reflects a broader risk-off environment and stretched valuations, said Dhruv Bhatia, Fund Manager - Equity at Edelweiss Asset Management."After a strong rally in the past months, stocks with weaker earnings profiles have been most exposed when sentiment turned, and liquidity tightened," he said. "The market is now demanding more reasonable valuations to justify higher discounting rates and clearer earnings delivery before the rally restarts."Read more: RBI governor reiterates listing requirement for top NBFCs as focus intensifies on Tata Sons Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) net bought shares worth ₹887.65 crore on Friday. Their total net sales in October so far total ₹51,466 crore, compared with exits worth Rs44,012 crore in September. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), meanwhile, remained net buyers of equities worth ₹3,235 crore Friday, taking their net purchases this month to Rs 59,110 crore. The India VIX, the market's volatility gauge, rose 6%, indicating heightened uncertainty in the near term."Fundamentally, September quarter results have come in line with or ahead of expectations, but the future looks uncertain due to higher oil prices and fiscal deficit along with rupee volatility," Shah said. Brent crude oil prices have climbed to $114.31 per barrel, marking a rise of about 6% in the last week.
